- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% if price is falling sharply.  
- If model shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce forecast 10–20% in the following 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If true price deviates >10% from forecast in first 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: next forecast = previous forecast + 0.5×(true - forecast).  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently >10% above true price, reduce by 1–3% per day for next 5 days unless sentiment is strong.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8 → 0.0 → 0.8), model may overreact; dampen forecast volatility by 15–20% in next 7 days.
